concept.name: Optimistic rollup
concept.definition: An optimistic rollup is a layer-2 rollup that assumes offchain transaction batches are valid by default and relies on a fraud-proof scheme: anyone can challenge a posted state transition during a challenge period, and proven fraud reverts the batch and slashes the operator's bond.
concept.intuition: It is an honor system with a bounty: transactions are accepted unless someone can prove cheating within a week, and the cheater's deposit pays for the mistake.
concept.mechanics: A sequencer batches transactions, posts them to Ethereum (calldata/blobs) with a new state root, and a challenge window (typically ~7 days) opens. Challengers re-execute the disputed step via an interactive bisection protocol settled by an L1 verifier contract; a successful fraud proof rolls back the invalid state and slashes the operator. Withdrawals to L1 must wait out the challenge period.
concept.failure_modes: Security rests on at least one honest watcher submitting fraud proofs — if all watchers fail or are censored, a malicious operator can steal funds; the 7-day withdrawal delay harms UX and pushes users toward trusted fast-exit bridges; centralized sequencers can censor.
concept.misconceptions: Optimistic rollups are not 'less secure versions of Ethereum' in the fraud-proof model — one honest node suffices to defend correct state — but most deployments still have training wheels (upgradeable contracts, permissioned provers). 'Optimistic' refers to the validity assumption, not speed.
concept.example: A user withdrawing 5 ETH from Arbitrum to Ethereum initiates the exit on L2, waits the ~7-day challenge period, then finalizes on L1; alternatively a liquidity provider fronts the 5 ETH immediately on L1 for a fee.
